detailed_description: Base58 Encoder/Decoder converts text to and from a Base58 string in the browser using the standard alphabet that omits 0, O, I, and l. Paste text or a Base58 string into the textarea, then click Encode to UTF-8 encode the input and convert it to Base58 (preserving leading zero bytes as leading 1 characters), or Decode to parse a Base58 string back into bytes and decode them as UTF-8. Invalid Base58 characters during decoding show an error message. The output appears in a read-only textarea with a Copy button, and Clear resets both fields. The shown alphabet is for reference only. The tool does not validate Bitcoin or other cryptocurrency address checksums (Base58Check), handle binary file input, support Base58Check or alphabet variants, or sign or verify keys.
usage_steps: Paste plain text or a Base58 string into the input textarea
Click Encode to UTF-8 encode the input and produce a Base58 string
Or click Decode to convert a Base58 string back to UTF-8 text
Read the output textarea or the inline error if the input contains characters outside the alphabet
Click Copy to copy the output, or Clear to reset both fields
Refer to the displayed alphabet panel to check which characters are valid
usage_examples: Encode a short identifier into a Base58 string that avoids look-alike characters
Decode a Base58 string back into the original text to inspect what it represents
Round-trip a sample value through Encode then Decode to confirm the alphabet handles it
Check why a pasted Base58 string fails to decode by reading the invalid character message
